bounds.domain: One host-controlled account directory, three configuration filenames in source order, one selected credential string and at most two migration calls. The middle file is initially credential-free or invalid; the first and last require scrubbing. A host can repair the rejected middle file between calls.
bounds.publication: A private temporary write precedes per-file atomic rename. Migration changes an original file only on successful rename; effect and acknowledgement settle together. Failures leave earlier successful rewrites visible. Missing files and parsed credential-free files share the retained equivalence class.
limitations: No lock or cancellation API exists here. A single trusted host serializes migration against other writers. Concurrent writers, symlink replacement races, hostile parent directories, multiple processes, crashes, fsync durability and applied-but-unacknowledged rename are outside this projection. Rejected calls may leave private temporary files; cleanup is not modeled.

The real disk scenarios exercise local/cloud/profile namespace selection, private modes, nested object/array scrubbing, preserving other strings and non-selected files, malformed JSON repair/retry, symlink/directory/oversized-file rejection and idempotent clean retries. This is named conformance, not exhaustive TypeScript or filesystem refinement.

Credentials use symbolic equality in the model. Real namespace tests call the source SHA256 derivation and prepare private directories. The model does not cover namespace creation/chmod failures, hash collisions, external verification, authorization or downstream host composition. Configuration inputs in the scrub projection are JSON objects; arbitrary JSON root values and arbitrary nesting are not proved.

The source is a documented native-host composition entrypoint. This repository calls namespace preparation in its real child-process test; no in-tree runtime calls credential scrubbing. Migration success does not establish that a downstream host invoked it or that old credentials are removed from unrelated files or substring values.

assumptions: One host serializes calls and performs only the explicit malformed-file repair. Other writers cannot restore scrubbed credential values. No fairness is required for this action safety property.
The failure outcome precedes rename publication; a lost rename reply after the effect is outside the finite outcome projection. No fairness is required. Earlier committed files remain visible.

Weak fairness of settle represents eventual success or rejection of every admitted filesystem operation and fair continuation. It does not require a retry, successful disk operation, host repair, elapsed-time deadline or scheduler refinement.
No fairness is assumed. An admitted disk operation or local continuation may stutter forever; the expected result requires a temporal loop counterexample.
